newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds drift, unmoved by credit data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds drift, unmoved by credit data.

text.p: Irish government bonds shed early gains in afternoon trade on Thursday as the market took a cautious stance ahead of domestic credit data which left the market unmoved after their release, dealers said.

''The market was very well bid, pushing ahead quite strongly following good U.S. overnight,'' a dealer said. ''We ran into profit taking at the higher levels ahead of the Central Bank credit figures. ''
Dealers said the monthly statistics from Ireland's Central Bank, released at 1630 GMT, had no discernible impact on the market, but would probably bias the market towards giving a better bid price.

The Central Bank data showed end-January private sector growth up at 15.2 percent from 14.7 percent at end-December. Residential mortgage lending was very slightly lower than in January 1996 resulting in a slight drop in the annual rate to 14 percent from 14.1 percent in December.

By 1730 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 30 pence from Wednesday's close at 102.22 to yield 5.92 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was flat from the close at 109.65 to yield 6.58 percent.
The spread in the 10-year bond had tightened by about two basis points on Thursday, reflecting good demand for Irish bonds, dealers said.
''On the short side things have stabilised - we've cheapened up there quite a bit but we're not out of the wide ranges against Germany the way we are with the 10-year.''
''Like everyone else we're looking ahead to the non-farm in the U.S. tomorrow," the dealer added.
